text:
ops-bot: INCIDENT-3219: PAGE to oncall (rodrigo). Severity: P1. Symptom: repeated container restarts in us-east-1 GPU pool during prefill path. Error spike ~07:02 UTC. Impact: ~7% 5xx on /v1/generate, elevated tail latency.

rodrigo (oncall): ack, joining. pulling logs now. which pool and model?

anna (sre): us-east-1-azb-3 pool. Container id abc123 restarted 8x in last 6m. Logs show CUDA OOM during prefill. Example: `RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Device 0. free 1.9GB, requested 3.2GB`. Prefill tokens observed ~120k for one request (req-9876).

matt (runtime): model involved: `gpt-large-rlhf-quantized-v2` with KV cache. We saw one oversized request with seq_len ~120384 that caused a massive prefill allocation. Prefill batch size for pool was 12 → big aggregate.

anna (sre): snippet: ```stderr: 2026-03-17T07:01:12Z RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Traceback (most recent call last): ... Prefill tokens: 120384 ReqID: req-9876 container: abc123```

matt (runtime): mitigation options (quickest first):
1) apply router-side truncation for requests >40k tokens (hotpatch routing rule)
2) immediately reduce prefill batch limit for this pool from 12→4
3) enable fallback routing for large-context requests to coldmodel (CPU) or smaller model variant
4) evict KV cache aggressively on this pool and increase reserved mem buffer

rodrigo (oncall): which is fastest to reduce restarts and customer errors?

matt (runtime): fastest = combination of #1 + #2. Router rule push ~3-5m. Batch limit change is config change 1-2m to apply. Fallback routing needs more validation (~30m).

anna (sre): I'm going to reduce batch limit and increase spawn_throttle now to prevent rapid restarts. Command: `curl -X POST https://control-plane/api/pools/us-east-1-azb-3/config -d '{"batch_limit":4,"spawn_throttle_ms":5000}'`

ops-deploy-bot: change cfg-20260317-azb3-batch applied to 6 nodes — rollout started.

ellie (support): drafting customer-facing update. Will say: intermittent errors for large-context requests, mitigations in progress, ETA ~15m. Tagging top affected tenants for manual follow-up.

customer-ops: please add note that some very long requests may be truncated; offer retry guidance.

matt (runtime): prepping router hotpatch to drop/persist any prefill >40k tokens and route to coldmodel or smaller-quant variant. Patch ready; request approval to push. Patch id: rtr-hotfix-3219.

rodrigo (oncall): approve. Push it.

ops-bot: router-hotfix rtr-hotfix-3219 rollout started.

ops-deploy-bot: router-hotfix rtr-hotfix-3219 successfully applied to edge routers in us-east-1 (6/6).

anna (sre): monitoring metrics: error rate dropping from 7% → 1.2% over 10m. Container restarts stopped after batch limit change and router patch. CPU coldmodel fallback saw small bump, within expected range.

ellie (support): customer update sent to affected tenants at 07:25 UTC. One tenant requested logs and SLA impact summary; forwarding to security/compliance.

matt (runtime): notes for follow-up: add long-window alerting (prefill token > 50k), implement automatic per-request cap (soft limit + prompt to client), and improve KV cache eviction heuristics to avoid fragmentation on big prefills. Also consider per-tenant limits for context length.

rodrigo (oncall): summary for handoff to night: hotpatch applied, batch limit reduced, monitor for 2 hours. If error rate creeps above 2% or restarts resume, page runtime and infra. Handoff to lisa in 30m.

lisa (oncall): ack. I'll watch the pool and dashboards. Please leave notes about which tenants were impacted and the req IDs to trace.

rodrigo (oncall): leaving handoff. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
